fig1_heat_wave.svg: Finite-difference solutions (solid) versus the separated mode (dots) for the fundamental $u(x,0)=\sin(\pi x)$. Top: heat_1d (FTCS) decays as $\sin(\pi x)\,e^{-(\pi/L)^2 t}$, matching heat_mode. Bottom: wave_1d (leapfrog at Courant $C=1$) keeps the shape but its amplitude swings as $\cos(\pi t)$, matching wave_mode — parabolic decay versus hyperbolic oscillation from the same initial data.
fig2_laplace.svg: Steady-state solution of $\nabla^2 u=0$ on the unit square with the top edge held at $u=1$ and the other three at $0$, relaxed with laplace_2d (Gauss-Seidel: each interior point becomes the average of its four neighbours). White curves are isopotentials. With no time derivative the field is harmonic — the same boundary-value problem as the electrostatic potential and steady-state temperature.
